While the basic premise of the story—a working-class woman marrying into a wealthier family with an intimidating mother-in-law—could easily have fallen into predictable tropes, the execution is entirely original and free of clichés. Instead of making Miss Emily a cartoonishly evil snob who tries to sabotage the marriage or pay off the bride, the story presents her as a complex, pragmatic, self-made businesswoman. Furthermore, the prose avoids overused expressions in favor of fresh, specific observations (such as a breaking bottle making a "hopeful sound first," or wealth being described as "the ability to prepare for occasions that hadn’t happened yet"). The relationship between the narrator and her mother-in-law develops with quiet, realistic nuance rather than relying on melodramatic or predictable plot points.
